payload_or_id.description: admin.py's update_value() persists the new value via Storage.put() but never calls Cache.evict() (or otherwise invalidates) the corresponding cache entry, even though Cache.evict() exists in cache.py specifically for a writer to call after an update. Cache.get() never re-checks storage for a key it already has cached, so any reader who already has the key cached keeps getting served the pre-update value until the evictor's TTL pass happens to remove it.

evictor.py computes now = time.time() in seconds but compares it directly against Entry.inserted_at_ms, which is stored in milliseconds, with no unit conversion. now - entry.inserted_at_ms is therefore always a large negative number and never exceeds TTL_SECONDS, so the 'expired' condition is never true. run_eviction_pass never evicts any entry, silently disabling the cache's only bound on both size and staleness.

get_value() can return a value that no longer matches what was last written to storage, and does so as an ordinary successful response -- counted under kvstore_get_value_requests_total{outcome="success"} -- with no signal to the caller that the value is stale. Bounded to a TTL_SECONDS (300s) staleness window if the evictor is working; in the current build (see kvstore_evictor_ttl_unit_mismatch) eviction never fires, so the staleness is actually indefinite for the life of the process.

Because eviction never fires, the in-process cache dict grows by roughly one entry per unique key ever requested, with no upper bound. Under sustained unique-key traffic this exhausts process memory, degrading latency or crashing the process for all clients -- not just the ones requesting keys with stale data.

Storage persists entries as one 'key,value' line per record and parses each line with line.partition(","), splitting on only the first comma, with no escaping or quoting of the delimiter character in either the key or the value.

Because the storage format doesn't escape commas, a key containing a comma is parsed back as a different, truncated key on readback, and Storage.put()'s existing-entries dict -- keyed by that same truncated parse -- can merge two logically distinct keys into one stored line. Writing key "foo,bar" can silently corrupt or overwrite the value stored under plain key "foo", and vice versa, with no error raised on either the read or write path -- the client believes both operations succeeded.

event.text:
All six `failure_modes` entries were accepted into phase 2 for this delta:

**Root causes (internal, not directly observable — excluded from alerting, chained instead):**
- `fm-kvstore_write_path_no_cache_invalidation` (warning) — `update_value()` never invalidates the cache entry it just made stale.
- `fm-kvstore_storage_unescaped_delimiter_format` (warning) — the flat-file store's `key,value` format has no escaping for the comma delimiter.

**Root causes with a real detection gap (critical, metric-gap):**
- `fm-kvstore_evictor_ttl_unit_mismatch` (critical) — the evictor compares seconds against milliseconds, so eviction never fires. Recommended fix: an `entries_evicted_total`/eviction-pass counter that would flatline visibly.

**User-visible leaves (each `caused_by` the roots above, all metric-gap):**
- `fm-kvstore_stale_value_served` (warning) — `get_value` silently returns stale data, indistinguishable from a correct hit in the existing `outcome=success` counter. Needs a served-value-age signal.
- `fm-kvstore_cache_unbounded_growth` (critical) — unbounded cache growth from the evictor bug, eventually OOMs/degrades the whole process. Needs a cache-size gauge.
- `fm-kvstore_storage_key_collision` (critical) — comma-bearing keys silently corrupt/overwrite unrelated keys on disk. Needs delimiter-violation detection at the storage boundary.

Each entry carries a `coverage_status` (`excluded` with reasoning, or `metric-gap` with a concrete instrumentation recommendation) per the "every failure mode ends in an alert or a reasoned exclusion" principle — the actual alert rules themselves are phase 4's job, not proposed here. Let me know if you want me to move on to drafting those metric/alert recommendations.

Repair needed in phase 4: unmapped_failure_mode (fm-kvstore_evictor_ttl_unit_mismatch); unmapped_failure_mode (fm-kvstore_stale_value_served); unmapped_failure_mode (fm-kvstore_cache_unbounded_growth); unmapped_failure_mode (fm-kvstore_storage_key_collision). Propose edits via propose_edits tagged for these phase(s), then call run_control with amend_complete when the repair is done.

payload_or_id.title: Evictor is not evicting any entries
payload_or_id.condition: A new counter, e.g. kvstore_evictor_entries_evicted_total (incremented once per key removed in run_eviction_pass), stays at 0 across eviction passes for longer than a few TTL_SECONDS windows (e.g. sum(increase(kvstore_evictor_entries_evicted_total[30m])) == 0 sustained for 1h) while the process has been up longer than TTL_SECONDS.
payload_or_id.rationale: This directly catches the seconds/milliseconds unit bug (or any future regression that disables eviction) before it manifests as unbounded memory growth or permanently stale reads -- it observes the root cause instead of waiting for a downstream symptom.

payload_or_id.title: Served cache values exceed the staleness budget
payload_or_id.condition: A new age signal, e.g. a histogram/gauge of (now - Entry.inserted_at_ms) sampled on each cache hit, shows p99 served-value age above TTL_SECONDS (300s) sustained for 15m.
payload_or_id.rationale: The existing kvstore_get_value_requests_total counter cannot distinguish a correct hit from a stale one -- both count as outcome="success". A dedicated age signal is required before staleness can be alerted on at all; without it this failure mode is invisible until a human notices wrong data.

payload_or_id.title: Cache entry count growing without bound
payload_or_id.condition: A new gauge, e.g. kvstore_cache_entries (sampled from len(Cache._entries)), either exceeds an absolute threshold sized to the process's memory budget, or shows sustained monotonic growth with no plateau/drop over a multi-hour window (which a correctly evicting cache would never do under steady-state unique-key traffic).
payload_or_id.rationale: Unbounded growth silently degrades or crashes the whole process for every client, not just ones reading stale keys -- this is the highest-impact symptom of the evictor bug and needs its own page-worthy signal in addition to alerting on the evictor root cause.

payload_or_id.title: Delimiter-bearing key detected at the storage boundary
payload_or_id.condition: A new counter, e.g. kvstore_storage_delimiter_violations_total, incremented whenever Storage.get/put is called with a key or value containing the ',' delimiter, fires an alert on any nonzero rate (threshold > 0, no sustained window needed).
payload_or_id.rationale: Any occurrence silently corrupts or overwrites an unrelated key's data with no error on either the read or write path, so this should page immediately on first occurrence rather than wait for a rate threshold -- there is no safe volume of silent data corruption.
